$comment: Exemption registry for the provider-token-shape guard (HMA-16). One entry per file deliberately retaining lines that match the CRED_TOKENPATS shape set. `expectedHits` is the exact count of matching lines the file is allowed to carry - the non-reversible discriminator; entries never carry a matched value. Reasons are a closed vocabulary: byte-literal-fixture (the file is consumed as raw bytes, so the token cannot be assembled at runtime), historical-record (CHANGELOG/docs text that must not be rewritten), escalated (requires a recorded-decision ledgerRef). Entries for .ts/.js/.mjs/.tsx paths are rejected unless escalated: those lines are rebuilt with the runtime-assembly idiom instead (see __tests__/types/credential-format.test.ts). Enforced by __tests__/hardening/token-shape-guard.test.ts via __tests__/helpers/token-shape-guard.ts.

entries.note: Release-history prose quoting synthetic fixture shapes (0.25.x false-positive notes and the credential-patterns 0.1.1 pin rationale). Rewriting shipped changelog text would falsify the record.

The VHS demo lab writes these bytes into throwaway lab files (.env, index.js) via quoted heredocs so the recorded demo scan has something to detect. Assembling them at runtime would obscure the documented lab content without changing what lands on disk.
Insecure-by-design fixture scanned as raw bytes by the scanner suites; JSON has no runtime assembly.
Insecure-by-design MCP config fixture scanned as raw bytes; JSON has no runtime assembly.
Insecure-by-design .env fixture scanned as raw bytes; dotenv files have no runtime assembly.
